TextExpander is a very practical keyboard shortcut tool that has just launched a free plan, allowing users to access its core Snippets feature on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows and Chrome. Details below.

TextExpander launches free plan

I've written before that TextExpander is one of the first apps I install every time I get a new Mac.

Over the years, I've built up a library of about 200 Snippets (that's TextExpander's name for text abbreviations that automatically expand into pre-written text), most of which I use regularly to quickly reply to emails, fill out forms, prepare podcast outlines, write sponsor reads, write show notes, and more.

While macOS's native text replacement has been steadily improving, features like variable support, conditional sections, nested Snippets, and math macros make TextExpander an indispensable tool for me.

TextExpander recently launched a free plan. According to the company speaking to 9to5Mac, the plan offers 5 active Snippets, unlimited library storage, unlimited text expansions, and up to 5 team members. The free plan also works on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome, and the same Snippet library syncs across all devices.

Honestly, the 5 Snippet limit may feel quite restrictive, especially since the free plan only lets you swap out one active Snippet every two weeks.

However, this can also be a great way to ease into TextExpander—keep shorter, simpler text replacements handled by macOS, and save the longer or more complex Snippets for TextExpander.

For more information about the TextExpander free plan, click here.
